title: 2013 AMC 10A Problem 7
statement: A student must choose a program of four courses from a menu of courses consisting of English, Algebra, Geometry, History, Art, and Latin. This program must contain English and at least one mathematics course. In how many ways can this program be chosen?

solutions.text:
English is required, so choose the other \(3\) courses from the \(5\) courses Algebra, Geometry, History, Art, and Latin.

There are \(\binom53=10\) such choices, but one of them, History-Art-Latin, contains no mathematics course.

Therefore the number of valid programs is \(10-1=9\).

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: English is fixed, so choose three of the five remaining courses
Count all three-course choices from the remaining courses, then remove the choice with no math
